risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Ship recycling economics are closely linked to steel prices; significant fluctuations in domestic and international steel prices can affect vessel acquisition prices, realisations and operating margins
- Availability of vessels for recycling is influenced by freight rates, second-hand vessel prices, newbuilding activity and global shipping conditions; strong freight markets may encourage shipowners to keep operating older vessels, reducing recycling volumes
- Changes in global trade, geopolitical tensions, disruptions to shipping routes and fluctuations in freight rates can materially influence vessel deployment and recycling decisions
- Compliance with evolving environmental, health and safety regulations may require continued investment in infrastructure, technology, waste management and employee safety, raising operating and capital expenditure
- Competition from other major ship recycling destinations, particularly Bangladesh, Pakistan and Türkiye, may affect vessel procurement and pricing
- International vessel transactions may involve foreign currencies; exchange-rate fluctuations can affect acquisition costs and overall profitability
- Company-flagged concerns include shortage of labour, rising manpower and material costs, approval/procedural difficulties, and lack of adequate sources of finance
- Risks are rooted in the industry's inherent dependence on global trade and the cyclical nature of related sectors like oil, natural gas, shipping and transportation; the offshore industry continues to be in a trough

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Prudent procurement and strategic timing of ship purchases to build inventory for future profitability
- Focus on operational efficiency
- Focus on regulatory compliance
- Focus on environmental stewardship
- Focus on occupational health and safety
